purpose:
This report presents consideration of
the objections received following statutory consultation on the
proposed TRO amendment to extend Zone H to include Dixwell Road
(south of Sandgate Road), Cliff Road, Metropole Road East and West,
and The Leas (between Earls Avenue and Metropole Road
West).
content:
This report presents consideration of
the objections received following statutory consultation on the
proposed TRO amendment to extend Zone H to include Dixwell Road
(south of Sandgate Road), Cliff Road, Metropole Road East and West,
and The Leas (between Earls Avenue and Metropole Road
West). 
 


DECISION:

1.   
To receive and note Report
C/26/08.

2.   
That officers proceed with the making of the
proposed amendment TRO, and implement
the associated changes at the earliest opportunity.

3.   
That, in light of the
representations received, the operational hours for the
restrictions along the section of The Leas be amended to 11am to
5pm, all days.

4.   
That the new restrictions are subject to an
operational review 18 months after implementation.

 

 
 


Reasons for decision:

 

The Cabinet Member for Transport is asked to agree
the recommendations set out below because:

Overall, the parking changes will deliver a well-balanced and
equitable outcome, ensuring fair consideration for residents,
visitors and businesses.
They will significantly improve parking availability and
accessibility for residents, allowing them to park more
conveniently near their homes, without overlooking the requirements
of other users.
They will improve traffic flow and road safety by reducing
obstructive parking and supporting more orderly vehicle
movement.
Seasonal charges from April to September will discourage long
stay parking by non-permit holders, improving access for visitors,
including free parking for Blue Badge holders in shared use
spaces.
Most residents living on these roads have expressed strong
support for introducing parking controls.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Transport has decided to extend parking restrictions in certain areas to improve parking availability and accessibility for residents, visitors, and businesses.

This report outlines the
government’s recent local plan reforms and asks Cabinet to
approve an updated timetable for the preparation of the

content:
This report outlines the
government’s recent local plan reforms and asks Cabinet to
approve an updated timetable for the preparation of the
council’s new local plan. Delegated authority is sought to
publish key documents that will enable the council to begin early
stages of the new local plan for the district, now that regulations
to the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act have been
published.
 

DECISION:
 
1.         
To receive and note report C/26/06.
2.         
To approve the receipt of Local Plan Implementation
Funding to support the council’s local plan process.
3.         
To approve the 2026 Local Plan Timetable included in
Appendix 1 for publication and submission to MHCLG as
necessary.
4.         
To delegate authority to the Chief Officer Planning and
Building Control to update the 2026 Local Plan Timetable on a
monthly or more frequent basis and publish and submit the updates
throughout the preparation of the local plan.
5.         
To delegate authority to the Chief Officer Planning and
Building Control to publish the council’s notice of intention
to begin plan-making.
6.         
To delegate authority to undertake the ‘scoping
stage’ consultation to the Chief Officer Planning and
Building Control, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Otterpool Park and Planning
Policy.
7.         
To delegate authority to the Chief Officer Planning and
Building Control to publish the Gateway 1 self-assessment, and any
other necessary supporting evidence, and submit to MHCLG as
necessary.
8.         
To note that Cabinet approval will be sought for the
statutory consultation on the proposed local plan content and
evidence.
9.         
To delegate authority to the Chief Officer Planning and
Building Control to approve, publish and submit the gateway 2
assessment materials and publish the appointed person’s
advice.
10.     
To note that Cabinet approval will be sought for the
statutory consultation on the proposed local plan.
11.     
To delegate authority to the Chief Officer Planning and
Building Control, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Otterpool Park and Planning Policy, to
approve any changes to the local plan following comments received
during the statutory consultations at the proposed local plan
content and evidence and proposed local plan stages.
12.     
To delegate authority to the Chief Officer Planning and
Building Control to approve, publish and submit the gateway 3
assessment materials and publish the appointed person’s
advice.
13.     
To delegate authority to the Chief Officer Planning and
Building Control to submit the local plan to the Secretary of State
for examination once gateway 3 is successfully completed.
14.     
To delegate authority to the Chief Officer Planning and
Building Control, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Otterpool Park and Planning Policy, to
make any necessary main modifications to the local plan and to
consult on the main modifications.
 

 

Reasons for
decision:
 
To meet the requirements of the
new plan-making system for local plans prepared under the
Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023 and to comply with new
plan-making regulations.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to approve an updated timetable for the preparation of the new local plan in response to recent local plan reforms.

set out in this report.
content:
This
report provides a draft proposal for the allocation of community
grant funding in the 2026-27 General Fund Revenue Budget. The
report also includes a proposed amendment to the Ward Budget Scheme
(Ward Member Grants) Terms and Conditions. Community
Grants represent a strategic investment in our voluntary
sector that improves lives, strengthens neighbourhoods, and reduces
pressure on statutory service. OSC considered the report on 7April
2026 and were in favour of the schedule. Their key points are also
set out in this report.

DECISION:

1.         
To receive and note report C/25/95.

2.         
To approve changes to the member ward grant scheme and to
approve the recommended grant allocations as set out in the 26/27
grants schedule.

3.         
To agree that longer term grant agreements be issued to key
bodies as set out in section 5.5 of this report.

4.         
To note that the discretionary grant allocation may be needed to
top up grant recipients in relation to fuel costs, but that
available funds can be promoted through a number of means as set
out in section 5.2 of this report.
 

Reasons for
decision:
 
The Cabinet Member for Communities is asked to
agree to the recommendations, as set out below, because agreement
is needed on allocating grants to community organisations in
accordance with the 26/27 grant schedule attached.

purpose:
This report presents the
findings of the recent informal parking consultation regarding
proposals to extend the Controlled Parking Zone (CPZ) operational
hours and to convert the existing parking bays to ‘permit
holders only’ at Radnor Cliff and Radnor Cliff Crescent,
Sandgate, during the April–September period. The full

The recommendations are based on the responses

content:
This report presents the
findings of the recent informal parking consultation regarding
proposals to extend the Controlled Parking Zone (CPZ) operational
hours and to convert the existing parking bays to ‘permit
holders only’ at Radnor Cliff and Radnor Cliff Crescent,
Sandgate, during the April–September period. The full
analysis of the consultation is outlined in Appendix 1.
The recommendations are based on the responses
received.

DECISION:
1.         
To receive and note
Report C/25/86.
2.         
That,
subject to a formal statutory consultation on a proposed Traffic
Regulation Order (TRO) amendment, the following changes be
progressed:
a. Conversion of
Bays:
That the existing shared?use parking bays within the identified
section of Radnor Cliff and Radnor Cliff Crescent be converted to
permit holders only during the period April to
September.
b. Passing
Places and Bay Adjustments:
That the proposed design incorporates the creation of additional
passing places, achieved by shortening selected marked bays to
improve vehicle flow, and that these passing places be marked with
yellow lines and kerb markings.
c. Extended
Operational Hours:
That the operational hours for the relevant bays be extended from
8:00am–6:00pm to 8:00am–8:00pm during the
period April to September.
d. Inclusion of
Lower Radnor Cliff:
That the lower section of Radnor Cliff be included within the scope
of the proposed changes.

3.       That the
council’s highway engineer report back to the Cabinet Member
for Transport if there are any objections to the proposed TRO
amendment.

 

Reasons for
decision:
 
The Cabinet Member for Transport, Regulatory Services and
Building Control is asked to agree the recommendations
because:
 
a)                 
The responses received
indicate that the majority of respondents are in favour of
extending the CPZ operational hoursand
converting the spaces to ‘permit holders only’ during
the period April to September.
 
b)                 
The changes will help
improve traffic flow and reduce parking challenges commonly
experienced by residents between April and September.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Transport has decided to extend the Controlled Parking Zone operational hours and convert parking bays to 'permit holders only' at Radnor Cliff and Radnor Cliff Crescent during the April-September period.

decision_maker: Leader of the Council and Cabinet Member for Otterpool Park and Planning Policy
purpose:
This report seeks approval for
the Council to enter into a time-limited Planning Agreement with
Homes England. The outcome of this activity will secure the outline
planning consent, enable early housing and support the future
delivery of Otterpool Park.
content:
This report seeks approval for
the Council to enter into a time-limited Planning Agreement with
Homes England. The outcome of this activity will secure the outline
planning consent, enable early housing and support the future
delivery of Otterpool Park.

DECISION:
 
1.         
To receive and note report C/25/49.
2.         
To note the draft
Heads of Terms and governance arrangements which will frame the
detailed drafting and negotiation of the Planning
Agreement.
3.         
To note that the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee Task & Finish Group have been
consulted and are supportive of entering into an Agreement, noting
the draft Heads of Terms and governance
arrangements.
4.         
To agree that the
Councilprogresses the
detailed drafting and negotiation of,
and then subsequently enter into, the
Planning Agreement with Homes England based on the draft Heads of
Terms detailed in this report.
5.         
To agree to
delegate authority to the Chief Executive, in consultation with the
Leader, to progress the detailed drafting and negotiation of, then
subsequently agree the final terms of the Planning
Agreement.
6.         
To note that the
outcome from the work undertaken through the Planning Collaboration
Agreement will be reported to Cabinet as part of future reports on
progress to secure additional investment and a strategic joint
venture partner to deliver the New Garden
Town.
7.         
To note that the
activities of the OP LLP will continue to be contained within an
annual Transition Plan with a supporting budget reported to
Overview and Scrutiny Committee and Cabinet until such time that
the council makes a further decision on the
matter.
 
 

 

Reasons for decision:
 
This report follows an earlier
decision in December 2024 (Report C/24/61) agreeing that the
Council enter into a Collaboration Agreement with Homes England
aimed at securing the delivery of Otterpool Park. 
Entering into a further agreement, which is focused on securing
outline planning consent and enabling early housing delivery, is a
key step in continuing the Council’s collaborative working
with Homes England.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to progress a Planning Agreement with Homes England to secure outline planning consent and enable early housing in Otterpool Park.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Transport, Regulatory Services and Building Control
purpose:
This report presents the findings
of the recent informal parking consultation regarding proposals to
extend Zone G1 to include Hasborough Road, Varne Road, and Varne
Place. The recommendations are based on the responses
received.
content:
This report presents the findings
of the recent informal parking consultation regarding proposals to
extend Zone G1 to include Hasborough Road, Varne Road, and Varne
Place. The recommendations are based on the responses
received.

DECISION:
1.       
To receive and note Report C/25/44.
2.       
That the parking proposals are not progressed
3.       
That officers continue to monitor parking in the area and report
any new developments to the Cabinet Member for Transport
 

Reasons for
decision:
 
The Cabinet Member for Transport, Regulatory
Services and Building Control is asked to agree the recommendations
set out below because:
a)              
The responses received indicate that the majority of respondents
are not in favour of introducing parking controls.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Transport has decided not to progress parking proposals for Hasborough Road, Varne Road, and Varne Place.
